android.desc:
StepMania is a rhythm game that lets players create and play custom content. Since 2008, the AMX edition has focused on expanding the simulator's capabilities while maintaining compatibility with existing content.

Over the years, the project has accumulated thousands of improvements and bug fixes. It was also the first version to introduce features that are now common across most simulators, such as independent BPM changes for each difficulty and Pump It Up-style hold notes, as well as experimental features that continue to evolve, including speed areas and the timeline fold model.

Our goal is to bridge the past, present, and future of the StepMania ecosystem by reducing the need to maintain multiple simulator versions for different content packs. To achieve this, a single installation aims to reproduce content from the last three decades as faithfully as possible, whether it uses DivX or HEVC video, AIFF or AAC audio, BMP or WebP images, or KSF or SSC step data.

Location: Mexico City
  Remote: Yes
  Willing to relocate: No
  Technologies: TypeScript (Node.js + React), Redux, GraphQL
  Résumé/CV: https://www.linkedin.com/in/aldomx/
  Email: aldomx@gmail.com

Who I am

Software developer, 30+ years of coding (18+ professionally). Started as a kid modding PC and Arcade games, and still doing that today: currently porting a WinXP-era game to mobile with the help of LLMs. That legacy codebase, with all its tech debt and ancient bugs, has taught me more about AI-assisted development than any professional project: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.amx.stepmania

What I've done

Led the migration of a 30M MAU website to TypeScript to cut production incidents from null-safety issues. Worked across PHP, .NET, Java, but gravitated to TypeScript/Node/React. I'm the person who doesn't wait for overseas teams to answer, and reads the code across a .NET Core backend, a Java/Spring payment service, and a bespoke Java microservice. LLMs lower the barrier, but it doesn't disappear.

What I'm looking for

Long-term remote role (ideally 5+ years). A team where knowledge sharing is a habit, not a nice-to-have. Where "why are we doing X?" is welcomed, and where ADRs come from real conversations instead of LLM auto-gen.
